name: What is the difference between a walk-in shower and a roll-in shower?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a walk-in shower and a roll-in shower?

acceptedAnswer.text: A walk-in shower typically features a low curb of two to four inches, whereas a roll-in shower has a completely flush, zero-threshold entry. Walk-in units work well for individuals who can step over a slight lip, but they still present a trip hazard for wheelchairs or walkers. Roll-in showers require lowering or sloping the subfloor to ensure water drains properly without a barrier. While zero-threshold designs require more extensive framing, waterproofing, and custom tile work, they provide long-term barrier-free access that accommodates wheelchairs easily.
acceptedAnswer.description: Walk-in showers have a low curb you must step over, while roll-in showers feature a zero-threshold entry flush with the floor for wheelchair and walker access.
